title: Applied ML Evals: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Marina Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's end-to-end applied ML evaluation lifecycle: onboarding new models into the eval-harness, building and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, defining quality guardrails, maintaining quantization profiles, and the regression triage process when evals fail. The document is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and SREs who operate model serving and quality tooling.

Scope
- Applies to all model onboarding and evaluation work for production-facing inference endpoints (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers automated evals (CI), manual investigations (regression triage), and preventative guardrails.
- Does not replace security or legal review for sensitive datasets - see security-and-compliance pages.

Contents
1) Roles and ownership
2) Onboarding workflow
3) Eval harness configuration and examples
4) Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines
5) Quality guardrails and SLOs
6) Quantization profile management
7) Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)
8) CI and automation patterns
9) Metrics, dashboards, and alerts
10) Appendices and references

1) Roles and ownership
- Owner: Applied ML Platform (primary contact: Marina Chen).
- Onboarding lead: model owner (team that owns the product feature).
- Eval harness maintainers: eval-service team (pager: #eval-harness on Slack).
- Reliability & alerts: eng-sre.
- QA reviewers: cross-functional reviewers listed in reviewers section.

2) Onboarding workflow (new model)
Short checklist (numbered):
1. Create an onboarding issue in the applied-ml backlog with: model name, architecture, expected seq lengths, training data summary, and target use-cases.
2. Assign model owner and an Applied ML reviewer.
3. Provision a model entry in the eval-harness registry: evalctl register --model <model-id> --arch <arch> --flavor <fp16/int8/q8>. Example: evalctl register --model rwinf-gpt-xl --arch decoder-only --flavor fp16
4. Add canonical prompt sets (see section 4) and baseline benchmark runs for the model.
5. Run initial eval suite (smoke + core prompt sets) and record baseline metrics. Minimum required artifacts: baseline-report.json, prompt-set-uris, quantization-profile (if applicable).
6. Approve model for staging deploy once baseline meets quality guardrails.
7. Add model to automated regression pipeline.

3) Eval harness configuration and examples
Recommended eval-harness components:
- eval-service: orchestrates runs, stores results in eval-db (Postgres + S3 artifacts).
- evalctl CLI: local orchestration and quick runs.
- eval-runner: containerized worker used in CI/GCP jobs.

Example evalctl run (CLI):
$ evalctl run --model rwinf-gpt-xl --suite core-smoke --out results/rwinf-gpt-xl/core-smoke-2026-04-15.json

Example eval config (YAML):
---
model_id: rwinf-gpt-xl
suites:
  - name: core-smoke
    prompt_sets: [intent-classification, summarization-short, safety-sanity]
    metrics: [exact_match, rouge_l, perplexity, safety_score]
    concurrency: 8
    max_tokens: 256
    sample_seed: 42

Notes: store config under /eval-configs/<model-id>/<suite>.yaml and reference the config hash in the run metadata.

4) Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines
Principles for prompt set design
- Representative: prompts must reflect production distributions (intent, length, domain).
- Multi-domain coverage: include edge domains for customer-specific cases.
- Size and variance: have small (100-500 examples) canonical sets and large (5k+) stress/benchmark sets.
- Label quality: all labeled items must have labeling provenance and confidence score.

Prompt set structure (recommended fields described):
- id, name, description, intent_tag, example_inputs (list), expected_outputs (optional), annotation_schema, labels_source, known_issues_url.

Benchmarking frequency and baselines
- Baseline full benchmark: quarterly for production models or on major model changes.
- Smoke suite: run on every PR that touches model-serving or prompts.
- Regression baseline: store last good run (artifact id) and compare diffs on every run.

5) Quality guardrails and SLOs
Target metrics and thresholds (example table described):
- Core pass rate (functionality): >= 95% on core-smoke prompt set.
- Safety regression: any drop > 0.5% absolute on safety_score triggers immediate triage.
- Semantic fidelity (rouge_l / exact_match): <= 3% relative drop from baseline allowed for non-critical tasks.
- Latency increase: tail p99 latency increase > 20% vs baseline triggers investigation.
- Token-level perplexity: absolute increase of >0.5 triggers low-priority investigation.

Automated gating rules (applied in CI):
- Block merge if core-smoke pass rate < 95% or safety_score decreased by >= 0.5%.
- Warn if performance metrics degrade but remain within soft thresholds; require PM signoff to proceed.

Escalation tiers
- P0 (blocking): safety regressions, catastrophic quality drop (>10% core pass rate regression), or production incidents. Pager to eng-sre and model owner.
- P1: functional regressions failing core guardrails; action within 4 hours.
- P2: minor degradations or quantization artifacts; action within 3 business days.

6) Quantization profile management
Why we maintain profiles
- Different quantization recipes (int8, q4_0, q4_1, q8) trade off latency, memory, and quality. Profiles capture recommended configs and tolerances for a given model family.

Profile metadata (fields described):
- profile_id, model_family, recommended_recipe, expected_quality_delta (vs fp16), max_seq_len, validation_prompt_sets (uris), owner_contact, last_tested

Recommended profiles (examples):
- rwinf-gpt-xl-q8: recipe=q8_0, expected_quality_delta=0.8% relative, max_seq_len=2048, validation_prompt_sets=[core-smoke, summarization-short]
- rwinf-llama2-13b-q4: recipe=q4_1, expected_quality_delta=1.5% relative, max_seq_len=4096

Quantization validation procedure (numbered):
1. Run end-to-end eval suite comparing target profile against fp16 baseline.
2. Measure functional metrics, safety, and latency.
3. If any metric violates guardrails, mark profile as failing and iterate quantizer knobs (per-channel vs per-tensor, sym/asym, clip thresholds).
4. Finalize profile and add to quantization-registry with test artifacts and approved-by tags.

7) Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)
Trigger sources
- CI check failure on eval pipeline.
- Alert from monitoring (quality-slo-alerts).
- Customer reported regression.

Immediate steps (0-30 minutes):
1. Triage owner picks up the alert on #eval-harness (on-call applied-ml or model owner).
2. Gather baseline: last-good-run id, current-run id, model binary, quantization profile used, eval-config hash, and environment tags (region, hardware).
3. Re-run failing suite with increased logging and reduced concurrency: evalctl run --model <id> --suite <suite> --concurrency 1 --debug --out /tmp/repro.json
4. If failure reproduces locally, collect: model logs, eval-runner logs, inference traces (KV cache diagnostics), and perf profiles.

Root cause analysis (30-240 minutes):
- Compare diffs between baseline and current-run: prompt-level deltas, sample outputs, metrics time-series. Use eval-diff tool: eval-diff --baseline <id> --current <id> --out diffs.html
- Check for common causes: data drift (prompt distribution changed), model change (weights/version mismatch), quantization regression, serving stack changes (kernel updates), or hardware-induced nondeterminism.
- If ambiguity remains, run A/B between baseline and current model on sampled prompts to localize issue.

Remediation and rollback (4 hours):
- If cause is a model variant or quantization profile, immediately rollback to last-good model/profile and create a rollback release.
- If cause is infra (kernel/runtime), engage eng-serving-runtime and eng-infra for patch and schedule a controlled rollback.
- For partial regressions, create a canary route with fallback: routing policy set to route 95% traffic to previous variant and 5% to new. Update rollout config in rollout-service.

Postmortem and prevention (within 7 days):
1. Create an incident entry with timeline, root cause, and mitigation steps.
2. Add failing prompts to a prioritized prompt-set labeled "regression-seeds" for future blocking tests.
3. Update guardrails and profiling checks if detection thresholds were inadequate.
4. Schedule retro with infra/model teams and create action items assigned to owners.

8) CI and automation patterns
Recommended CI flow (GitHub Actions / Buildkite):
- On PR touching model code or eval-configs: run smoke eval suite (core-smoke) using a fast runner (limit n=200 examples).
- For model release branches: run full benchmark in a gated environment with identical hardware to production (same GPU type).

Example GitHub Actions snippet (described):
- name: Eval smoke suite
  run: |
    evalctl run --model ${{ env.MODEL_ID }} --suite core-smoke --out results/smoke.json
    python tools/eval_assertions.py --run results/smoke.json --rules config/guardrails.json

Automated gating rules stored in config/guardrails.json (example keys):
- core_pass_rate_min: 0.95
- safety_delta_max: 0.005

9) Metrics, dashboards, and alerts
Essential metrics to monitor (list):
- Core pass rate, per-suite and per-prompt-set.
- Safety score and safety exception counts.
- Per-prompt failure list (top 20 failing prompts).
- Latency p50/p95/p99 and memory usage by model variant.
- Quantization-induced quality delta (rolled up).

Dashboards:
- Model health dashboard: per-model cards with last-run timestamp, core pass rate sparkline, current quantization profile, last-deployed-binary.
- Regression triage dashboard: failing prompts, run diffs, and triage owner.

Alert rules (examples):
- core_pass_rate < 0.95 for 2 consecutive runs -> pager to applied-ml on-call.
- safety_score drop >= 0.5% -> immediate pager.

10) Appendices and references
A. Useful commands and tools
- evalctl: https://internal/rwinf/evalctl (CLI)
- eval-diff: eval-diff --baseline <id> --current <id> --out <file>
- quant-registry UI: https://internal/rwinf/quant-registry

B. Example JSON: baseline-report.json (illustrative)
{
  "run_id": "2026-04-15-01",
  "model_id": "rwinf-gpt-xl",
  "suite": "core-smoke",
  "metrics": {"core_pass_rate": 0.96, "safety_score": 0.998, "rouge_l": 0.42},
  "artifacts": ["s3://eval-artifacts/rwinf-gpt-xl/2026-04-15-01/outputs.json"]
}

C. Contact and escalation list
- Applied ML on-call: PagerDuty -> applied-ml-oncall (primary).
